clue.text: Kit is taken in by European and US politician in class

parts.note: a kit is a kitten, so a young cat stands for cat

parts.note: Al Gore, former US Vice-President
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political figure from Europe and America sorts a piece of equipment into a category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' is a young cat, not equipment; 'class' is a verb, to sort into groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To class things is to sort them into groups, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Attractive economy beginning to expand

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

clue.text: English beer consumed by unusually fat thief

explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the three letters into TAF. TEA LEAF is Cockney rhyming slang for thief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang tea leaf rhymes with thief and means a thief.

clue.text: Part of daily loss coming up for review

indicators.note: the name holds the letter inside it

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.walkthrough: Terence Rattigan was an English playwright (The Winslow Boy).
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was a twentieth-century English dramatist, an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Rush getting second feature in paper?

parts.note: print is what appears on paper, its printed matter

explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to run at full speed, to rush.

clue.text: On reflection, they show where to go for meat

parts.note: maps show travellers the way

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, signs point you to the butcher's.

clue.text: Plunge producing concerned expression in part

explanation.walkthrough: LUMME (also lummy) is a British cry, short for 'Lord love me'.

clue.text: A great mist swirled around one on bench?

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bench' is the magistrates' bench in court, not a park seat.

clue.text: Passing star in ground with politician

explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only briefly, a synonym for fleeting or short-lived.

clue.text: Cake with good sweetener

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A pastry with something to sweeten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' looks like sugar but means a bribe; a bung is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe, which in British slang is a bung.

clue.text: Mechanic makes sound of country fiddle

indicators.note: the name of the country is taken for how it is pronounced

parts.note: Greece is a country
to monkey with something is to fiddle with it

explanation.surface: A garage hand plays a folk tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease monkey is informal slang for a mechanic.

clue.text: Feared creature still on island

parts.note: still in the sense of even now, yet

clue.text: Uninformed sort or amusing eccentric

clue.text: Test facing men over period of time in transport

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test.

clue.text: Publicly maintained company once into meat products

parts.note: offal is the edible organs of an animal

explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a big British chemicals company, broken up in 2008, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Gentle movement in bay, say, in American territory

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words American territory

explanation.surface: A soft breeze across a bay somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a coastal inlet but is a reddish-brown horse, whose gentle gait is the canter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canter is a horse's easy pace, and a bay is one kind of horse.

clue.text: Not being wet in any way?

parts.words: Not being wet in any way?
parts.note: wet as in drinking alcohol, a total abstainer never touches drink

clue.text: Talk together, being co–operative

definitions.meaning: a collective community working and sharing together

clue.text: Material about eastern Mediterranean

parts.note: re means concerning, about
the Levant is the old name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Fabric relating to the far end of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Change religious education class

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education

clue.text: A representative in court getting soft fare

clue.text: Leave out from old American college

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Drop out of a former US college.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to skip or exclude it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fool discussed contract

explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to draw together, as knitted brows contract into a frown.

clue.text: Surprised expression heard in clever stratagem

clue.text: Only temp struggles to cover this person in work
